proof_summary: Quadratic reciprocity makes 5 a square modulo such a prime; choosing an even root \(e\) and setting \(n=e-1\) gives an odd \(n<p\) with \(p\mid (n+1)^2-5\) (with \(p=11\) handled directly). Writing the continued fraction as a ratio of adjacent terms of a second-order recurrence, a Casoratian/factorial identity and prime-power valuation bounds show that the entire cofactor of \(p\) cancels with the adjacent term, while recurrence propagation shows \(p\) itself cannot cancel, so the reduced denominator is exactly \(p\).
